transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18 | 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Gomez (Acme Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Priya Singh (Security), Jon Park (Product)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie with Redwood, this is Samir, our SE, and Evelyn from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta: Doing well, thanks. We set aside an hour to walk through what a POC would look like, specifically around deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private — cause we have, uh, strict latency and data rules.
[00:18] Samir: Great, that's exactly what we're hoping to scope today. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, get workload sizing (QPS, concurrency, seq len), propose benchmark plan and timeline, and then map to deployment recommendations.
[00:30] Liam: Sounds good. For context — we run user-facing personalization APIs behind our storefront. Peak traffic is around 400 RPS, typical burst to 900 for flash sales. Latency target is 200ms p95 end-to-end for the text-gen path.
[00:44] Jamie: 200ms p95 end-to-end, ok. What's your acceptable backend inference p95?
[00:49] Jon: Ideally sub-100ms if possible, but we can tolerate up to 150ms inference p95 with caching.
[00:55] Priya: From security side, all inference logs must not leave our VPC. PII must be redacted. We also need KMS-managed keys and SOC 2 evidence.
[01:06] Samir: Got it. Quick questions on model: are you planning to use a smaller distilled model or something larger? That impacts deployment.
[01:12] Marta: We're evaluating a 7B open model for now, then a 13B if quality requires it. Most sequences are short — 40-80 tokens — but we have some longer sessions up to 512 tokens for multi-turn dialogues.
[01:24] Samir: Perfect. For workload sizing I'll note: steady 400 RPS, burst 900 RPS, avg seq length 60, some 512s. Any concurrency constraints on your side?
[01:34] Liam: Backend concurrency limit is 200 concurrent requests.
[01:38] Samir: Good. Now success criteria — what would you consider a successful pilot?
[01:42] Marta: Three things: 1) match or improve quality compared to our current in-house model (we have baseline evals) — no more than 2% regression on our eval set; 2) meet latency target — end-to-end 200ms p95 during baseline load and under 300ms p95 during bursts; 3) predictable cost estimates within 10% of forecast.
[02:01] Jamie: Clear. So initial POC scope: run a 3-week benchmark with synthetic traffic mirroring your peak and long-tail, measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens; then run a 1-week pilot with shadow traffic on a subset of users — does that align?
[02:16] Marta: Yes. Timeline wise we're hoping to decide by early October if we go Dedicated. So a 4–6 week POC now would fit.
[02:25] Samir: Implementation notes: for Hosted mode, we can spin up Redwood API endpoints immediately — great for speed. For Dedicated, we'd reserve GPU pools; autoscale and burst to handle flash sales. For Private, we'll need to schedule on-prem or VPC control plane provisioning — leads to longer setup (3–6+ weeks).
[02:44] Jon: Can Dedicated satisfy the 'logs must not leave our VPC' requirement?
[02:48] Samir: Dedicated keeps compute on our infra but data routing varies — we can support private peering and customer-side VPC peering; we also support a Private deployment which fully isolates the control plane and keeps logs in your environment. For strict data residency the Private deployment is the safest, Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering and log forwarding to your SIEM but may still touch Redwood control plane metadata.
[03:10] Priya: We need KMS integration and HSM-backed key storage for model assets; is that supported in Dedicated?
[03:16] Samir: Yes, Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed KMS. For Hosted, we can support envelope encryption but customers with regulatory needs usually opt for Dedicated or Private. We'll share our KMS integration doc.
[03:29] Marta: What's the estimated cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our workload?
[03:33] Jamie: Ballpark: Hosted per-token is simplest but at your sustained throughput Dedicated often reduces unit cost by 30-50% depending on utilization. There's also a fixed reserved capacity commitment for Dedicated. We'll send tailored numbers but expect Dedicated to look better once you commit to steady baseline.
[03:50] Liam: For Dedicated, how do you handle autoscaling for flash events — does it cross-region?
[03:56] Samir: Autoscale can be configured with burst capacity and cross-pool fallback; if your traffic spikes beyond reserved GPUs we can route to compatible model variants (e.g., lower precision) to maintain availability. We use batching and KV cache for prefixes to reduce per-token work when you have repeated prompts.
[04:16] Marta: You mentioned quantization. Will quality drop significantly if we use 4-bit quantized models?
[04:21] Samir: It depends on model and eval — for many 7B models 4-bit quant can be near-lossless, for some 13B models there's a small hit. Part of the POC is to run quantization profiles and compute quality vs cost curves.
[04:36] Jamie: Ok let's talk benchmarks. Samir, what's your proposed plan?
[04:40] Samir: Step 1: a 3-day synthetic benchmark on our side using your sample prompts — measure throughput (tokens/sec), p95/p99 latencies, and failure rate across Hosted and Dedicated configs. Step 2: a 1-week shadow run with a percentage of live traffic to validate end-to-end. We'll provide a harness and a script; we'll need access to a sample production prompt set and a small eval set.
[04:59] Jon: What metrics should we expect in the report?
[05:02] Samir: We'll report p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, batch sizes, cache hit rates, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also run an accuracy regression against your eval set.
[05:15] Marta: For the initial synthetic runs, can we test both Hosted and Dedicated with the same model weights and quantization?
[05:20] Samir: Yes, we'll keep model variants consistent so the only variables are infra and runtime config.
[05:24] Jamie: On timeline: we can get Hosted benchmark started within 48 hours of you sharing prompts. Dedicated requires a little setup — reserve GPUs and configure access — estimate 7–10 business days to be benchmark-ready. Private would be 3–6 weeks depending on provisioning and network approvals.
[05:41] Liam: That is a key decision driver. If Dedicated is ~10 days and Private 3–6 weeks, we could start Hosted to get early numbers and then run Dedicated in parallel so we don't block decisioning.
[05:52] Samir: Absolutely. We often run parallel Hosted and Dedicated bench to show delta.
[05:57] Priya: Security questions: do you provide audit logs, SSO integration, RBAC?
[06:01] Jamie: Yes: SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs are available. For Private you can push logs to your SIEM and maintain them in your account. We'll attach our security pack (SOC2, ISO certs).
[06:12] Priya: Great. Also need contract language around data residency and breach notification timelines.
[06:17] Jamie: Noted — legal can prep a data processing addendum and we can share SLAs.
[06:21] Marta: One more on cost: do you have tooling to estimate per-route cost?
[06:26] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route estimates — we can demo that during the pilot. Caching and batching recommendations can also be applied to reduce unit cost.
[06:36] Jon: If we find regression in quality after quantization, what's rollback look like?
[06:40] Samir: We support model pinning and rollbacks. For Dedicated you can host both quantized and full-precision variants and route traffic accordingly; automatic fallback is also possible if SLOs are missed.
[06:52] Marta: Ok summarizing success criteria: quality within 2% regression, end-to-end p95 <=200ms baseline and <=300ms burst, cost predictable within 10%. POC timeline 3-week bench + 1-week shadow, decision by early Oct.
[07:07] Jamie: Sounds good. Action items: we'll send pricing and security docs, Samir will send benchmark harness and timeline, Priya to confirm docs required. We'll schedule the benchmark run for next week pending prompt set.
[07:20] Liam: One small note — we use internal feature flags; during shadow run we'll toggle for 5% of users.
[07:25] Samir: That's perfect for real traffic validation.
[07:28] Marta: Anything else?
[07:30] Evelyn: I'll open the follow-up thread with calendar invites and link to the shared Drive with the harness.
[07:35] Jamie: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items we listed.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had some mislabels; speakers confirmed names in chat. Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-summary.pdf and sample benchmark harness at https://drive.example.com/redwood-acme-harness

End of meeting.
